# skey — API keys for AI agents

I found an open-source tool called skey. Please explain what it does for me and help me set it up with you. Everything about it is below.

Site: https://skey.tscodex.com · Tour: https://skey.tscodex.com/tour
npm: @tscodex/skey · GitHub: https://github.com/unbywyd/skey · License: MIT

## What it is

skey keeps API keys and passwords in the operating system's keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service). AI agents such as Claude Code use them by name — the value never enters the chat, so the agent never has to treat a key as leaked.

## What it can do

- Use a key by name: `skey run --only STRIPE_SECRET_KEY -- npm run sync`. The value goes only into that process's environment. If the program prints it back, the output shows `***MASKED***`.
- Ask for a key instead of "paste it here": `skey request "SMTP_PASS:Mailgun password" --note "where to find it"`. A local page opens with exactly those fields (or answer in the terminal with `skey fill`). Values go straight into the keychain; the agent continues by itself and sees only names.
- Get a key from someone on another computer: `skey request ... --share` prints a link. It is end-to-end encrypted in their browser (ECDH P-256 + AES-256-GCM); the relay sees only ciphertext; one reply per link; the link expires in 24 h. `--offline` works without any server: they send back an encrypted text, you run `skey import`.
- Move keys where they belong without reading them: `skey dotenv .env --only A,B`, `skey run --stdin NAME -- gh secret set NAME`, `skey run --only VAR=STORED -- cmd`.
- Manage keys in the browser: `skey ui` (names and dates only, never values). Clean up after a one-off transfer: `skey clean <request id>`.

## Install

Node 18+ on macOS, Windows or Linux:

    npx @tscodex/skey ui          # opens a local page to add your keys
    npm i -g @tscodex/skey        # or install the `skey` command globally

## The agent skill (Claude Code)

The skill teaches the agent to ask for keys with `skey request`, move them without reading, and clean up:

    mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/skey
    curl -o ~/.claude/skills/skey/SKILL.md https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unbywyd/skey/main/skill/SKILL.md

Then allow skey without approval prompts, but never reading or typing values. Merge into ~/.claude/settings.json:

    {
      "permissions": {
        "allow": ["Bash(skey run:*)", "Bash(skey list:*)", "Bash(skey request:*)", "Bash(skey wait:*)",
                  "Bash(skey dotenv:*)", "Bash(skey import:*)", "Bash(skey clean:*)"],
        "deny": ["Bash(skey export:*)", "Bash(skey set:*)", "Bash(skey fill:*)"]
      }
    }

`export`, `fill` and `run --no-mask` also refuse to work without a real terminal, so an agent cannot read a value even if a rule is missing.

## Limits, honestly

- `skey run` is not a sandbox: the command you run gets the secret.
- Masking catches the value and common encodings; a command that transforms the value first can still print it.
- A value written to a file with `skey dotenv` is a plain file.
- The shared page is served by the relay; if you do not trust it, answer from the terminal (`skey fill "<link>"`) or run your own relay.

1. In two sentences, tell me what skey would solve for me.
2. Check whether it is installed: `npx -y @tscodex/skey list`.
3. Offer to install the skill and the permission rules above, and show me how to store my first key.
